questions.question: R–X is the general formula of which functional group in which one or more hydrogen atoms are replaced by Group 17 elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Alkyl halides__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alkyl halides**, also known as** haloalkanes**, are organic compounds in which** one or more hydrogen atoms** in an** alkane** have been** replaced **by** halogen atoms** **(Group 17 elements** like** fluorine, chlorine, bromine or iodine)**.
 
• The formula for alkyl halides is **RX**, where **R** represents an **alkyl group** and **X **represents a **halogen atom (F, Cl, Br, I)**.
 
• **Naming** is based on the alkane name of the** longest carbon chain** attached to the halogen.
 
• The **IUPAC name** has the format** halo+alkane**, such as** chloromethane, bromoethane, etc**.
 
• **Common names** of alkyl halides consist of the name of the** alkyl group **plus the **first syllable of the name of the halogen**, with the ending -**ide**, such as **methyl chloride, ethyl bromide, etc**.
 
• Alkyl halides are widely used in organic chemistry as** intermediates in chemical reactions**, due to their reactivity towards **nucleophilic attack**.
 
• They also play a major role in the** industrial production of chemicals**.
 
• **Physical properties **such as boiling points of alkyl halides are influenced by factors like the **size of both the alkyl group and the halogen atom**, as well as the **degree of branching in the carbon chain**.
 
• Some example alkyl halides include:
 
 
• **Methyl Chloride (CH₃Cl)**
 
• **Ethyl Bromide (C₂H₅Br)**
 
• **Propyl Iodide (C₃H₇I)​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Organic compounds containing a** carbonyl group (C=O)** bonded to a nitrogen atom
 
• Commonly found in** proteins, peptides,** and** pharmaceuticals**
 
• Can be synthesized through the reaction of a **carboxylic acid with an amine**
 
• Have a wide range of applications in the **pharmaceutical**,** polymer,** and** agricultural industries**
 
 
 
• **Imines:**
 
 
• **​**Organic compounds containing a** carbon-nitrogen double bond (C=N)**
 
• Formed by the reaction of a **carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone) with an amine**
 
• Used as **intermediates **in **organic synthesis** and as** ligands in coordination chemistry**
 
• Can undergo** hydrolysis** to form a **carbonyl compound and an amine**
 
 
 
• **Nitriles:**
 
 
• Organic compounds containing a **cyano group (C≡N)**
 
• Used in the production of** synthetic rubber, plastics, and adhesives**

• Have applications in organic synthesis as** versatile intermediates** for the preparation of various compounds

questions.question: The Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) was launched by which Ministry of the Government of India during 2008-09?

options.text: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) is a credit-linked subsidy program.
 
• It was launched in 2008 for the generation of employment opportunities through the establishment of microenterprises in rural and urban areas.
 
• It is a central sector scheme being administered by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME).
 
• Implementing Agency at the National Level is Khadi and Village Industries Commission(KVIC).
 
 
• It is a statutory organization under the administrative control of the Ministry of MSME.
 
 
 
• Features of the scheme are as follow-
 
 
• It allows entrepreneurs to set up factories or units.
 
• Any individual above 18 years of age is eligible for this scheme.
 
• Only new projects/units are considered for sanction of loans.
 
• Maximum Cost of Project/Unit Admissible for Manufacturing Sector is Rs. 25 lakh.
 
• Maximum Cost of Project/Unit Admissible for Service Sector is Rs. 10 lakh.
 
• The government has decided to provide Subsidy in Rural Areas - 25% for the general category and 35% for the special category, which includes SC/ST/ OBC/Minorities, Northeast Region, Hill, and Border Areas. and, In Urban Areas- 15% for general category and 25% for special categories.
 
• Under the scheme, loans are provided by Public Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Co-operative Banks, and Private Scheduled Commercial Banks approved by respective State Task Force Committee.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises**, a** **branch of the **Government of India**.
 
• It is the **apex executive body** for the** formulation and administration of rules, regulations, and laws relating to micro, small and medium enterprises** in India.
 
• The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (M/o MSME) aims to cultivate a **vibrant MSME sector** by fostering its **growth and development**.
 
• The ministry's vision includes promoting sectors such a**s Khadi, Village and Coir Industries**, in partnership with associated Ministries/Departments, State Governments, and other stakeholders.
 
• To qualify as a Micro, Small or Medium Enterprise according to the MSME, an **enterprise's investment should not exceed Rs.50 crore** and its annual turnover** should not be more than Rs.250 crore**.
 
• **Key statistics and insights of MSME sector **are available through official surveys and reports, such as the** NSS 73rd Round Survey (2015-16)** and the **All India Census of MSME**.
 
• The Ministry oversees the registration of new **MSMEs**.
 
• There are** statutory bodies** and other offices attached to the Ministry, such as the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)**.

• The second five-year plan was for the year 1956-1961, this plan was based on the **Russian** model of industrialization.

__
 
• **Friedrich August Kekulé** was born on **September 7, 1829, in Darmstadt, Germany**.
 
• **Kekulé** became a** prominent chemist** in** Europe from the 1850s** until his death in 1896, making significant contributions especially in the field of organic chemistry.
 
• He is** best known for his work on the theory of chemical structure**, which describes the **arrangement of atoms within molecules**.
 
• **Kekulé proposed the cyclic structure** of **benzene **in **1865**, an idea reportedly inspired by a dream (or daydream) in which he saw a snake biting its own tail, a symbol known as the **Ouroboros**.
 
• This ring-shaped structural model for benzene revolutionized the understanding of organic compounds and marked a significant advancement in organic chemistry.
 
• **Kekulé passed away **on **July 13, 1896**, in **Bonn, Germany**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **compound was discovered in 1825 by English physicist Michael Faraday**. In modern times, it's primarily derived from petroleum.
 
• The benzene molecule is traditionally represented as a hexagon symbolizing six carbon atoms, and a circle inside the hexagon symbolizing a delocalized "pi system" composed of the p orbitals of the carbon atoms.
 
• The **structure of benzene **was first proposed by the renowned **chemist Friedrich August Kekulé in 1865**. This crucial revelation, that benzene was a cyclic structure made up of six carbon atoms in a ring with alternating single and double bonds
 
• Benzene is classed as an aromatic hydrocarbon, a class of compounds known for their distinctive fragrance and exceptional stability compared to other hydrocarbons. This stability is termed "aromaticity", a property ascribed to the delocalized pi electron system formed by overlapping p-orbitals over the ring.
 
• **Benzene is an important starting material **in the synthesis of a wide variety of chemical products, including** plastics, resins, synthetic fibers, rubber, dyes, detergents, pharmaceuticals, and explosives**.
 
• Despite its considerable utility in industry, benzene is known to be a carcinogen and is strictly regulated in many countries due to its negative environmental and health impacts.

questions.question: Which of the following is a rabi crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rabi crops or rabi harvests are crops that are sown in winter and harvested in the spring in India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.
 
• The term is derived from the Arabic word for "spring", which is used in the Indian subcontinent, where it is the spring harvest (also known as the "winter crop"). The opposite of the rabi crop is the Kharif crop which is grown after the rabi and Zaid (zaa-id) crops are harvested one after another respectively.
 
• The rabi crops are sown around mid-November, preferably after the monsoon rains are over, and harvesting begins in April / May.
 
• The crops are grown either with rainwater that has percolated into the ground or using irrigation. Good rain in winter spoils the rabi crops but is good for Kharif crops.
 
• The **major rabi crop in India is** wheat, followed by barley, mustard, sesame, and peas. Peas are harvested early, as they are ready early: Indian markets are flooded with green peas from January to March, peaking in February.
 
• Many crops are cultivated in both Kharif and Rabi seasons. The agricultural crops produced in India are seasonal in nature and highly dependent on these two monsoons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif Crops**:

 
 
• Kharif crops also are known as monsoon crops as they are cultivated in the monsoon season. These crops are sown at the beginning of the rainy season.

 
 
• Rice, **maize**, bajra, ragi, sorghum, soybean, **groundnut**, cotton, etc are all Kharif types of crops.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Zaid Season**:
 
 
• It is a short season between the Kharif and Rabi seasons. The crops grown during this season are known as Zaid crops.
 
 
• Pumpkin, cucumber, **watermelon**, bitter gourd, etc are all Zaid types of crops.

questions.question: At maturity, _____ is a non-conductive cell composed of heavily thick-walled dead cells with lignin and high cellulose content (60%–80%), and it serves to provide structural support in plants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Sclerenchyma cell.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• About **Sclerenchyma cells** 

 
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are plant cells that provide structural support to the plant. At maturity, these cells become non-conductive and composed of heavily thick-walled dead cells with lignin and high cellulose content (60-80%).
 
• The thick walls and lignin content make sclerenchyma cells rigid and durable, providing strength and support to the plant. 
 
• These cells are often found in tissues that need additional structural support, such as in the stems, roots, and vascular tissues.
 
 
 
• ​Reproductive cell: Reproductive cells are involved in the plant's reproduction process, including the formation of seeds and spores.
 
• **Parenchyma cell**: Parenchyma cells are versatile plant cells with thin walls. They are involved in various functions, including photosynthesis, storage, and secretion.
 
• Meristematic cell: Meristematic cells are undifferentiated, actively dividing cells responsible for plant growth.
 
• They are found in regions of the plant where growth occurs, such as the tips of roots and shoots. These cells are not non-conductive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**

There are mainly two types of plant tissues: **Meristematic Tissues and Permanent Tissues**. 

Meristematic Tissues : 

 
• ​Meristematic tissues are regions of actively dividing cells responsible for the growth of the plant. 
 
• They are **Found at the tips of roots and shoots (apical meristem), in the lateral buds (lateral meristem), and in between the xylem and phloem in stems (intercalary meristem).** **
 
• They contribute to the elongation of roots and shoots, formation of new leaves, and lateral growth of stems.

Permanent Tissues : 

 
• ​Permanent tissues are derived from meristematic tissues and have lost the ability to divide.
 
• Complex Permanent Tissues :
 
 
• Phloem: Composed of sieve tubes, companion cells, fibers, and parenchyma cells. Involved in the transport of food.
 
• Xylem: Composed of tracheids and vessels for water transport, and fibers for support. Also includes parenchyma cells.
 
 
 
• Simple Permanent Tissues:
 
 
• Sclerenchyma: Cells with heavily thickened, lignified cell walls, providing strength and rigidity to the plant. Found in mature stems, roots, and vascular tissues.
 
• Collenchyma: Cells with unevenly thickened cell walls, providing mechanical support to young plant parts like stems.
 
• Parenchyma: Cells with thin cell walls, involved in photosynthesis, storage, and secretion. Found in leaves, stems, and roots.

questions.question: Identify the organism that does NOT belong to the first level trophic level.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Zooplankton.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Zooplankton does NOT belong to the first level trophic level.
 
• Grass - Grass is a producer, belonging to the first trophic level. Producers are autotrophic organisms that produce their own food through photosynthesis.
 
• Phytoplankton - Phytoplankton are microscopic, photosynthetic organisms found in aquatic ecosystems. They are primary producers and belong to the first trophic level.
 
• Zooplankton - Zooplankton are small animals that feed on phytoplankton. As consumers, they belong to higher trophic levels and do not directly produce their own food.
 
• Trees - Trees are generally considered producers as they undergo photosynthesis to produce their own food. They belong to the first trophic level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Food Chain: A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms, each dependent on the next as a source of food. It represents the flow of energy and nutrients through different trophic levels.
 
• **Trophic Levels**: Trophic levels are hierarchical levels in an ecosystem, indicating the position of an organism in a food chain.
 
• The main trophic levels are producers (first level), consumers (herbivores and carnivores), and decomposers.
 
• Trophic levels represent the hierarchical levels in an ecosystem based on an organism's position in a food chain or web. 
 
• Each trophic level is defined by the organism's role in energy transfer and nutrient cycling within the ecosystem. 
 
• There are generally three main trophic levels : 
 
 
• ​Primary Producers (Trophic Level 1) : 
 
 
• These are autotrophic organisms, mainly plants, algae, and some bacteria. 
 
• They produce their own food through photosynthesis or chemosynthesis, converting sunlight or inorganic compounds into organic compounds.** **
 
• Energy sources are sunlight or inorganic compounds.** **Examples include** **Plants, algae, and certain bacteria
 
 
 
• Primary Consumers (Trophic Level 2) :
 
 
• Herbivores that feed directly on primary producers.** **
 
• They consume plants to obtain energy.
 
• Energy sources are Organic compounds produced by primary producers**. **Examples include Grazing animals, herbivorous insects.
 
 
 
• Secondary Consumers (Trophic Level 3) :
 
 
• Carnivores that feed on primary consumers.
 
• They consume herbivores or primary consumers for energy.
 
• Energy Source: Organic compounds obtained from primary consumers.
 
• Examples: Carnivores like foxes, snakes, and insect-eating birds.
 
 
 
• Tertiary Consumers (Trophic Level 4):Organisms: 
 
 
• Carnivores that feed on secondary consumers. 
 
• Role: They consume other carnivores.
 
• Energy Source: Organic compounds obtained from secondary consumers. 
 
• Examples: Apex predators like lions, hawks, or sharks.
 
 
 
• Quaternary Consumers (Trophic Level 5):Organisms: 
 
 
• Carnivores that feed on tertiary consumers. 
 
• Role: They consume other carnivores. 
 
• Energy Source: Organic compounds obtained from tertiary consumers. 
 
• Examples: Some top-level predators in specific ecosystems. 
 
 
 
 
 
• The 10% energy transfer law, also known as the "trophic level efficiency" or "energy pyramid," is a principle that describes the decrease in available energy as you move up the trophic levels in a food chain or web.
 
• According to this law, approximately 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.
 
• Here's how it works
 
 
• Producers (Plants): At the base of the food chain, plants (producers) capture sunlight through photosynthesis to convert it into chemical energy. They use a significant portion of this energy for their own metabolic processes.
 
• Primary Consumers (Herbivores): Herbivores consume plants to obtain energy. However, only about 10% of the energy stored in the plants is transferred to the herbivores. The rest is lost as heat during metabolism or used by the plant for growth and reproduction.
 
• Secondary Consumers (Carnivores): Carnivores that feed on herbivores receive about 10% of the energy stored in the herbivores. Again, the majority of the energy is lost in various processes.
 
• Tertiary Consumers (Higher-Level Carnivores): If there are tertiary consumers in the ecosystem (predators of the secondary consumers), they receive about 10% of the energy from the secondary consumers.
 
 
 
• This pattern continues, and at each trophic level, only around 10% of the energy is transferred to the next level. The rest is lost as heat or used for the metabolic activities of organisms at that level.The 10% energy transfer law is a fundamental concept in ecology and helps explain why food chains are relatively short and why ecosystems have a pyramid-shaped energy structure, with a broad base of producers supporting fewer consumers at higher trophic levels.

__

• Forest: While water in its liquid form (rivers, lakes) is commonly found in forests, the solid form (ice) is not as prevalent unless the forest is in a polar or high-altitude region.

• Liquid:
 
 
• Definition: In liquids, particles are closely packed but can move past each other, giving liquids a fixed volume but not a fixed shape.

questions.question: Who has cracked the Panini code in his thesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rishi Rajpopat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rishi Rajpopat, a Sanskrit scholar** of Indian origin who has successfully decoded a complex rule instituted by Panini.
 
• Panini was an ancient scholar considered to be the **father of linguistics**, who lived around 2500 years ago.
 
• Rajpopat's accomplishment is encapsulated in his academic thesis, **'In Panini, We Trust: Discovering the Algorithm for Rule Conflict Resolution in the Astadhyayi'**. 
 
• This groundbreaking work has reportedly resolved a problem that perplexed Sanskrit scholars for centuries, offering some groundbreaking insights into the algorithmic organization of the ancient language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panini’s system – 4,000 rules** detailed in the **Astadhyayi**, which was written around **500 BC** – is meant to work like a machine.
 
• Feed in the **base and suffix of a word** and it should turn them into **grammatically correct words and sentences** through a step-by-step process.
 
• Until now, however, there has been a big problem. Often, two or more of Panini’s rules are simultaneously applicable at the same step leaving scholars to agonise over which one to choose.
 
• Solving so-called **“rule conflicts”**, which affect millions of Sanskrit words including certain forms of “mantra” and “guru”, requires an algorithm. 
 
• Rajpopat’s research shows that Panini’s so-called language machine is also self-sufficient.

questions.question: Which field should be used when you want to send a copy of an email to someone else without the original recipient knowing?

__
 
• The BCC field stands for "**Blind Carbon Copy**".
 
• This field is used when the sender wants to send a copy of an email to other recipients without the main recipients knowing.
 
• This is often used for privacy purposes or when sending large-scale emails where it's more professional to keep each individual's email address private. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CC**:

 
 
• One can use the CC field (**Carbon Copy**) to send an email to additional recipients besides the primary recipient.
 
• However, all recipients will be able to see who else has received the email.
 
• Typically, one uses CC when all the recipients are equally relevant to the conversation, but no direct action is required from those in the CC field.
 
 
 
• **To**:
 
 
• This field is for the **primary recipient(s)**.
 
• They are the main intended readers and usually are the people from whom the sender expects some action or response.
 
• Multiple recipients can be added to this field, usually separated by semicolons.
 
 
 
• **From**:
 
 
• This field is used to identify the **sender of the e-mail**.
 
• This field should contain the e-mail address of the person or entity sending the e-mail.
 
• It is automatically filled when a person sends an email from their account.

• This is substantially higher than the **national average of 382 persons per sq. km**.
 
• Bihar is a landlocked state in the eastern part of India, and the third-largest state by population, after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.
 
• Even though Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India, it does not have the highest population density due to its larger area.
 
• Similarly, Kerala and Haryana, although having high population densities, are not as densely populated as Bihar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Census of India 2011 marked the **15th national census** of the country.
 
• It disclosed that India's total population was **1.21 billion**, an increase of 17.64% from the previous census in 2001.
 
• Notably, the sex ratio improved from 933 females per 1000 males in 2001 to 943 in 2011.
 
• However, there was a decline in Child Sex Ratio (0-6 years), from 927 in 2001 to 919 in 2011.
 
• The census revealed that there was an increase in literacy rate from 64.83% in 2001 to 74.04% in 2011.
 
• Despite housing less than 2.5% of the world population, India accounted for 17.5% of the global population.
 
• The population density increased to 382 persons per square kilometer.
 
• Another key finding was that the working-age population (15-59 years) increased from 58% in 2001 to 63% in 2011.

questions.question: Al Biruni wrote famous book “Kitab ul Hind” in __________ language.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Arabic.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-Ul-Hind and it was written in Arabic.**
 
• Kitab-ul-Hind is also known as **Tarikh-ul-Hind**.
 
• It is a comparative and critical study of **India's religion, culture, and society**.
 
• It is a voluminous text, divided into** 80 chapters **on subjects such as religion and philosophy, festivals, astronomy, alchemy, manners and customs, social life, weights and measures, iconography, laws, and metrology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Al-Biruni was a **Persian scholar and Polymath.**
 
• He was a scholar **appointed by Mahmud of Ghazni.**
 
• They have thrown a detailed light on Hindu religions and philosphy, festivals, customs and tradition, the social and economic as well as political life of the people. He is known for his unbiased views on the culture and customs of different nations.
 
• He is widely considered the **founder of 'Indology'.**
 
• Al-Biruni spent years in the company of Brahmana priests and scholars, learning Sanskrit, and studying religious and philosophical texts.
 
• He also wrote an encyclopedic work on India called** Taḥqīq mā li-l-Hind** (variously translated as A Critical Study of What India Says, Whether Accepted by Reason or Refused).
 
• He translated several Sanskrit works, including Patanjali’s work on grammar, into Arabic.

questions.question: According to Census of India 2011, how much per cent of the total population were Sikhs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.7%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the data from the 2011 Census of India, **Sikhs make up 1.7%** of India's total population.
 
• Sikhism is one of the most significant religions in India, primarily concentrated in the state of **Punjab**.
 
• It is India's **fourth-largest religious group**. 
 
• India's Sikh population stands at 20.8 million, which is only 1.72% of the country's total population.
 
• Out of approximately 25-30 million Sikhs in the world, the majority of them, 20.8-22 million, live in India which is about (83.2%-84.1%) of the world's Sikh population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindus** constitute the majority of India's population, with an overall share of **79.8%**.
 
• **Muslims** are the largest religious minority in India, amounting to **14.2% **of the population.
 
• **Christians** make up **2.3%** of India's population.
 
• **Sikhs** constitute **1.7%** of the population.
 
• **Buddhists** make up** 0.7%** of the population, while **Jains** account for** 0.4%**.
 
• 0.9% of the population follow other religions, including tribal faiths often categorized under 'Other Religions and Persuasions.'
 
• A small proportion, 0.2% of the population, did not state their religion.
